title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything — "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub:https://clianything.cc/
content:
Today's Software Serves Humans👨💻. Tomorrow's Users will be Agents🤖.
CLI-Anything: Bridging the Gap Between AI Agents and the World's Software
🌐 CLI-Hub: pip install cli-anything-hub then cli-hub install <name> — browse, install, and manage all community-built CLIs. Want to add your own? Open a PR — the hub updates instantly.
🎬 See Demos: Watch AI agents use generated CLIs plus preview, live preview, and trajectory loops to produce real artifacts — CAD builds, 3D scenes, diagrams, gameplay, subtitles, and more.
🙋 [Become a Contributor, or Request a CLI]: Join us! Sign up to build a new CLI harness — once reviewed and merged, you'll gain access as one of our community contributors! Wish CLI-Anything supported a specific software or service? Submit a wishlist request!
One Command Line: Make any software agent-ready for Pi, OpenClaw, nanobot, Cursor, Claude Code, etc. 中文文档 | 日本語ドキュメント | Deutsch

report.summary: HKUDS's CLI-Anything auto-generates command-line harnesses that let AI agents like Cursor and Claude Code operate virtually any software, backed by a community registry called CLI-Hub.
report.background: AI coding agents can write code but struggle to actually drive real application software — CAD tools, game engines, DAWs, GIS suites. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) addressed part of this, but every integration is bespoke, heavy, and often framework-specific. HKUDS (a Hong Kong University data science lab known for projects like LightRAG) bet on a simpler substrate: the command line. Their CLI-Anything project turns arbitrary software into scriptable CLI harnesses that any agent can call, with structured output, previews, and validation tests. Since launching its package manager in April 2026, the project moved to v0.2.0 with a progressive-disclosure HARNESS.md design, unified skill packaging, and a public registry that has merged dozens of community harnesses spanning creative, scientific, DevOps, and gaming tools.
key_points: One universal interface: CLI-Anything claims 'one command line' makes any software agent-ready for Pi, OpenClaw, nanobot, Cursor, Claude Code and similar agents. Instead of teaching each agent every GUI, the project exposes software through deterministic, testable CLI harnesses with preview and trajectory loops so agents can produce real artifacts.

CLI-Hub is a package manager for agent tools: `pip install cli-anything-hub` followed by `cli-hub install <name>` lets users browse, install, update, and uninstall community-built CLIs. Version 0.2.0 expanded install sources to pip, npm, brew, and bundled system binaries via a public_registry.json, with end-to-end install tests.

The merged harness catalog is broad and practical: QGIS (GIS mapping), Godot (game engine E2E pipeline), Unreal Insights, Kdenlive and Shotcut (video editing), Calibre (ebooks), Obsidian and Joplin (notes), Zotero (references), Rekordbox (DJ libraries), 3MF (3D meshes), Exa (web search), n8n and Dify (workflow automation), and CloudAnalyzer.

Skills and docs got a unified architecture: all SKILL.md files now live under a top-level skills/ directory installable via `npx skills add HKUDS/CLI-Anything --skill <name> -g -y`, and the v0.2.0 HARNESS.md redesign moved detailed guidance into on-demand guides/ files for progressive context loading.

Security and quality work is ongoing: untrusted XML/SVG/ODF/MLT/MusicXML parsing now routes through defusedxml, token-file handling was hardened against path traversal and symlink escapes, Rekordbox writes require backups, and DomShell added URL validation and DOM sanitization.
report.impact: For the AI industry, CLI-Anything is a pragmatic counterpoint to MCP maximalism: it argues the humble CLI, with plain stdin/stdout and text output, is already the ideal agent interface — cheap, composable, inspectable, and framework-agnostic. That lowers integration cost dramatically and could push more vendors to ship agent-ready command surfaces. For developers, it offers a contribution path and a reusable test/validation harness pattern, plus a registry to distribute tools. For regular users, it means natural-language control of professional software (CAD, video, GIS, music) without learning its UI — but also new risk: agents writing to real files and libraries, so backup discipline, sandboxing, and reviewing generated commands remain essential.
report.tools: Start with the CLI-Hub package manager (`pip install cli-anything-hub`, then `cli-hub install <name>`) and the web hub at clianything.cc. Browse the GitHub repo HKUDS/CLI-Anything for merged harnesses and the skills/ directory, install skills via `npx skills add HKUDS/CLI-Anything --skill <name> -g -y`. Pair it with agents like Cursor, Claude Code, Pi, OpenClaw, or nanobot, and compare approaches with MCP servers such as UEAtelier or safari-mcp.
